topics.title: Chapter overview
topics.summary: Compilation produces object code with references that linking must resolve. Static and shared libraries arrange that resolution differently, which changes deployment, update behavior, visibility, and compatibility obligations. Harbor’s scale operation is built both ways in the optional experiment so the executable contract stays constant while the packaging changes.

topics.title: 3.1.1 Archiving Object Files
topics.summary: A static library is commonly an archive of object files. Creating the archive groups compiled implementation units but does not generally resolve every external reference as a final executable link would. The eventual consumer still needs required dependencies and a compatible object format and ABI.

topics.title: 3.1.2 Linking Static Dependencies
topics.summary: The final linker selects code needed to satisfy references under the platform’s archive rules. Link order and cyclic dependencies can matter on some toolchains. Target-based dependencies make the intended relationships clearer, but they do not repair an incoherent circular architecture by themselves.

topics.title: 3.2.1 Understanding Dynamic Loading
topics.summary: A shared library is loaded or mapped as part of a process’s runtime environment, and symbols are resolved according to the platform’s loader rules. The executable must be able to locate a compatible library at runtime, not just while building. Search paths, runtime dependencies, and trusted installation locations are therefore part of deployment.

topics.title: 3.2.2 Managing Symbol Visibility
topics.summary: Export only the intended binary interface where the platform supports visibility controls. Hidden implementation symbols reduce accidental coupling and collisions, while Windows DLLs commonly use explicit import/export declarations. A public C++ header and a binary export list describe related but different interfaces.

blocks.text: `-fPIC` produces code suitable for relocation in a shared object. `-fvisibility=hidden` makes symbols non-exported by default; a production library would explicitly mark only supported API symbols for export. `nm -D` inspects the dynamic symbol table.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)
project(HarborLinkage LANGUAGES CXX)
include(CTest)
add_library(scale_static STATIC ../scale.cpp)
add_library(scale_shared SHARED ../scale.cpp)
foreach(target IN ITEMS scale_static scale_shared)
  target_compile_features(${target} PUBLIC cxx_std_20)
  target_include_directories(${target} PUBLIC "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/..")
endforeach()
target_compile_definitions(scale_shared PUBLIC HARBOR_SHARED PRIVATE HARBOR_BUILDING)
set_target_properties(scale_shared PROPERTIES CXX_VISIBILITY_PRESET hidden VISIBILITY_INLINES_HIDDEN YES)
foreach(kind IN ITEMS static shared)
  add_executable(test_${kind} ../main.cpp)
  target_include_directories(test_${kind} PRIVATE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/../../../support")
  target_link_libraries(test_${kind} PRIVATE scale_${kind})
  add_test(NAME ${kind}_contract COMMAND test_${kind})
endforeach()
